transcript:
Header: 2026-04-05 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45 mins | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Marco Diaz (CSM) -- Evergreen: Alice Chen, Ben Rosario, Karen O'Neill, Samir Patel

Summary: QBR / health check to review Q1 usage, cost drivers, reliability incidents, and evaluate Dedicated pilot. Jordan opens, Priya covers tech details, Marco handles ops/next steps.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time for the QBR. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Alice Chen: Hi Jordan, Alice here.
[00:10] Ben Rosario: Ben on the platform side.
[00:12] Karen O'Neill: Karen, product.
[00:14] Samir Patel: Samir, CTO.
[00:18] Priya Raman: Priya from Redwood, SE. Marco here too.
[00:22] Marco Diaz: Yep hi all.

[00:30] Jordan Lee: Cool. So agenda — usage & cost, reliability incidents, potential Dedicated pilot, security questions, then action items. Alice, do you want to kick off with how things trended Q1?
[00:45] Alice Chen: Sure, so Q1 we saw 2.6x growth in inference calls quarter over quarter. Most of the increase is longer sessions for our support bot and multi-turn conversation logs. Token counts per request up 40%. Costs are up accordingly, and we wanted to walk through tradeoffs.
[01:12] Ben Rosario: To add, our p95 latency is creeping during peak windows, especially when concurrency spikes. We currently run on hosted but with some burst to dedicated-ish pools, but we hit throttles last month.
[01:34] Priya Raman: Right, we saw a couple of throttling events in our logs; looks like you hit request burst limits tied to concurrency. With Redwood Dedicated we can reserve capacity to stabilize p95. Also Optimize can suggest batching and KV prefix caching to reduce token re-computation for repeated contexts.
[02:02] Karen O'Neill: Can you quantify savings? At least ballpark. Our finance team wants hard numbers.
[02:09] Jordan Lee: Absolutely. We'll share three scenarios — hosted w/ caching and batching, partially dedicated (reserve for peak hours), and full dedicated pilot. Each will show expected latency, % cost delta, and runway to break-even.
[02:26] Samir Patel: Important we include encryption and KMS details — our compliance team needs to verify keys never leave our KMS, and audit logs are a must.
[02:36] Priya Raman: Yes. Redwood Private with customer-managed KMS is an option; for Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS via the standard HSM/KMS connectors. We'll send the security pack.
[02:50] Ben Rosario: We also had one incident in March where inference returned partial responses for 18 minutes. Does Redwood have graceful fallback to a smaller model or region?
[03:02] Marco Diaz: We do—smart routing can fallback to a compatible model variant or another region if capacity drops. In that incident we saw a model OOM on the node, which triggered retries and a brief outage. We've since applied a kernel-level patch and changed autoscaling thresholds for similar workloads.
[03:28] Priya Raman: For long-running sessions, the KV cache is big win — avoids recomputing prefix tokens. We can show the delta in cost and latency in the follow-up benchmark.
[03:42] Alice Chen: Great. On security: SOC 2 is required, plus SSO via SAML. Any issues integrating with our IdP?
[03:50] Jordan Lee: No, we support SAML/SSO and RBAC. Priya will share the SSO integration guide.
[03:56] Karen O'Neill: Roadmap alignment — we have a product milestone end of Q2 that requires sub-200ms tail latency for the agent flow. Is that achievable with Dedicated?
[04:08] Priya Raman: Sub-200ms at p95 depends on model choice and sequence length; with a quantized model + Dedicated GPUs tuned for your sequence distribution and continuous batching tuned properly it's feasible. We'll need your seq length distribution and peak QPS to size the pool.
[04:28] Ben Rosario: We'll get you the peak QPS and distribution.
[04:33] Samir Patel: For the Dedicated pilot, what are the commitments and costs? We prefer a short proof-of-value before committing long term.
[04:40] Jordan Lee: We do month-to-month pilots for select customers, or one quarter reserved commit for better pricing. Jordan continues: We'll present both pilot and reserved options in the cost model.
[04:54] Priya Raman: Also, Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization and batching settings per workload; that usually gets 20-40% token cost reduction without visible quality loss. We'll include sample evals.
[05:08] Alice Chen: Any gotchas on data residency? We need EU-only processing for some segments.
[05:14] Marco Diaz: We can pin region routing and host model instances in EU regions; the control plane supports region policies. Private deployments can further ensure on-prem if needed.
[05:24] Ben Rosario: On the reliability incidents, can you share the postmortem?
[05:28] Priya Raman: We'll share the incident summary and what changed in infra: kernel patch, autoscaler tweak, and canary rollout adjustments.
[05:38] Karen O'Neill: On product roadmap, if we go Dedicated, what's the latency impact for the agent vs generator workloads — generator is big but can be async.
[05:47] Priya Raman: Generator can be batched and asynchronous which helps throughput but adds latency; agents need low tail latency and benefit from Dedicated single-request optimization and small-batch sizing. We'll show a matrix in the follow-up.
[06:05] Jordan Lee: Quick recap before we close — items: Redwood to send security pack + SSO guide, cost scenarios, and schedule a sizing/benchmark session. Evergreen to send seq length distributions and peak QPS.
[06:20] Alice Chen: Sounds good. Any blockers from our side? I think finance wants 2 scenarios: pilot and 12-month commit.
[06:28] Jordan Lee: We'll provide both.
[06:32] Samir Patel: Also please include an example SLA for Dedicated.
[06:36] Marco Diaz: We'll include the SLA language and escalation path.
[06:40] Jordan Lee: Awesome, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and booking invite.
[06:46] Karen O'Neill: Thanks all.
[06:48] Ben Rosario: Thanks.
[06:50] Meeting ends.
notes: Transcription contains minor mishears typical of call exports (some acronyms and product names may be slightly off). Shared artifacts referenced: QBR deck (link provided in follow-up), security pack, benchmark plan.
